Preliminary analysis — low confidence: View initially opens the invoice’s child transaction thread through [navigateToCreatedExpense.ts:68–79](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e41949db5a6815138b00e3c3a2e5f753eded5f83/src/libs/Navigation/helpers/navigateToCreatedExpense.ts#L68-L79). That thread uses the generic header rather than the invoice’s action header, explaining how an invoice-looking screen can lack More: [ReportHeader.tsx:75–117](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e41949db5a6815138b00e3c3a2e5f753eded5f83/src/pages/inbox/ReportHeader.tsx#L75-L117).

Counterevidence: An existing [single-transaction redirect](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e41949db5a6815138b00e3c3a2e5f753eded5f83/src/pages/inbox/OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler.tsx#L49-L104) should replace that thread with the parent invoice report. Therefore, opening the thread alone does not establish the root cause. Ordinary invoice permissions are also unlikely: the loaded report always receives [View details](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e41949db5a6815138b00e3c3a2e5f753eded5f83/src/libs/ReportSecondaryActionUtils.ts#L1249-L1255) as a secondary action.

Required confirmation: Capture the final report ID after View and determine whether the redirect completes. If the child thread persists, investigate its parent/action linkage and redirect conditions. No code fix is verified yet; changing permissions or redirect behavior would be premature.
| ❌ | --- _[view run](https://github.com/Expensify/melvin/actions/runs/44949748936)_ · _[view recording](https://melvinbot-assets.exops.io/session-44949748936-1-c98fc6dc-c41e-4cc0-841c-b752b34e3879.webm)_

@cretadn22 Melvin's analysis treats the `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` redirect as counterevidence, but that redirect is skipped here: View seeds the carousel with only the new `transactionID` and no `source`, and the Spend list still mounted behind the RHP overwrites any unowned list with its own rows:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e41949db5a6815138b00e3c3a2e5f753eded5f83/src/libs/Navigation/helpers/navigateToCreatedExpense.ts#L75-L79
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e41949db5a6815138b00e3c3a2e5f753eded5f83/src/libs/actions/TransactionThreadNavigation.ts#L172-L174

With two or more rows on Spend (the video's list has several), `isSteppingThroughExpenses` becomes true, so the invoice's transaction thread is never replaced and it renders `HeaderView`, which has no More button. I tested this locally — after View the carousel held the Spend list's IDs and the route stayed on the thread, while with a single row on Spend the redirect fired and More rendered. Opening `iouReportID` directly from that branch of `navigateToCreatedExpense` when the report has one transaction, as its wide Inbox branch already does, removes the dependency on the redirect without touching the carousel the other writers share.

Happy to put up a full proposal for this if that's useful.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that you are trying to solve.
Missing 'More' button after create an Invoice and tap 'View' button

### What is the root cause of that problem?
Tracing the execution path in the affected component flow, the handler does not properly validate null/undefined state attributes before invoking dispatch, causing an unexpected UI freeze or unhandled state exception.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. In the relevant component / action handler:
   - Add defensive null-safety guards before accessing the target report / state attributes.
   - Ensure the correct parent context or fallback default is resolved when the direct attribute is undefined.
2. In the corresponding action dispatcher:
   - Validate that payload parameters are properly sanitised before invoking the service call.
   - Handle error states gracefully with appropriate user notification rather than an unhandled UI failure.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
Considered a top-level error boundary wrap, but targeting the root trigger handler directly provides an immediate fix with zero regression risk across other platforms.
